sentences.text:
Mohd. Qayyum Gazi And 5 Others vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
on 21 July, 2023
Bench: Vivek Kumar Birla, Rajendra Kumar-Iv
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 20060 of 2022

Petitioner :- Mohd. Qayyum Gazi And 5 Others
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others

Counsel for Petitioner :- Dhiraj Kumar Upadhyay
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Rakesh Kumar Shukla,Seema Pandey
Hon'ble Vivek Kumar Birla,J.
Hon'ble Rajendra Kumar-IV,J.
1.

Heard Sri Dhiraj Kumar Upadhyay, learned counsel for the petitioners and learned A.G.A for the
State respondents and Sri Padmakar Pandey, holding brief of Sri Rakesh Kumar Shukla, learned
counsel for the informant.

2.  The relief sought in this petition is for quashing of the F.I.R. dated 2.7.2022, registered as Case Crime No. 08 of 2022, under Sections 147, 498A, 323, 427, 354, 354 (Kha), 506, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act and 5/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Jajmau, District Kanapur Nagar.

sentences.text:
Vide order dated 22.12.2022 the matter was referred to the Mediation Centre, however,
Mediation Report dated 2.3.2023 reflects that a sum of Rs. 30,000/- to be deposited by the petitioner was not deposited by him.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has refused to deposit the amount so directed by this Court vide order dated 22.12.2022.

5. By drawing attention to last paragraph of the order, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the informant that the present petition is liable to be dismissed for non-compliance of the order and cognizable offence is made out on bare reading of the FIR.

6. Last paragraph of the order dated 22.12.2022 is quoted as under:
"It is made clear that in case there occurs default by the petitioners either in depositing the amount or in appearing before the Mediation Centre on the date fixed,
the interim order shall cease to operate and the Mediation Centre shall immediately communicate with the office which in turn shall list the case within a week before the appropriate Bench for passing orders in the matter."
7.

In view of the aforesaid and after perusal of the first information wherein serious specific allegations have been levelled against the petitioners and as such, we find that cognizable offence is made out.

8. Therefore, in view of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana and others vs. Bhajan Lal and others, 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335 and M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt.
Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2021 SC 1918 and in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.3262/2021 (Leelavati Devi @ Leelawati & another vs. the State of Uttar Pradesh) decided on 07.10.2021, no case has been made out for interference with the impugned first information report.
9.
